items.en: When selecting a naval invasion order, the player will be asked to left-click on a province with a naval base as a point of departure and right-click on the enemy province(s) to invade. The army will automatically gather at the naval base they will depart from for the assault.
Enemy Trade law (Free trade: 20%, Export focus: 10%, Limited exports: 5%, Closed economy: 0%)

Radar coverage (Radars that cover ⟦0⟧ seazone with enemy ships on missions can provide up to 20% ⟦1⟧. Naval intel gathered per radar is only one value per country, not per seazone. Naval intel about the UK gathered per radar that covers the English Channel can provide ⟦2⟧ for a naval invasion in the Mediterranean Sea.)

Air superiority and ⟦0⟧ provide a bonus to ⟦1⟧. The maximum possible bonus from air superiority is +100% to the ship amount, making each ship count for two. It is achieved when air superiority is 100% and there are enough planes to cover 100% of the sea region.
Consider using Shore bombardment to support the invasion, as well as any ⟦0⟧ in range.

Unless invading divisions have captured a port or a city, they might be cut off from supply, and need to achieve these objectives within 72 hours before supplies run out. A floating harbor will provide a temporary supply hub in the landing province, giving the invaders a few weeks to secure an alternative supply source.

A paradrop is a battle plan order that uses ⟦0⟧ to land one or more paradrop-capable divisions onto a target ⟦1⟧. The paradrop order button is available in the battle plan toolbar for an army with at least one paradrop-capable division. After selecting the button, the player must left-click the province of an air base that contains a minimum of 50 transport planes and then right-click a province that is within transport range as the paradrop destination.

Executing a paradrop order requires sufficient transport planes for the number of divisions assigned to the order (by default, 45 planes per division) and either neutral or 70% air superiority in all required regions.

In order to be paradrop-capable, a division must contain only paradrop-capable battalions among its line battalions and support companies. Paradrop-capable divisions will have a checkmark on the parachute icon at the top left of the ⟦0⟧ window. Paradrop-capable battalions are indicated by a parachute symbol in their unit icons during battalion selection. Currently, only the ⟦1⟧ battalion is paradrop-capable as a line battalion. Paradrop-capable support companies are listed below; all other support companies are not paradrop-capable.

If the general commanding the divisions has the ⟦0⟧ commander trait, he will have access to the ⟦1⟧ ability, which decreases the transport plane requirement by 10% (i.e., base requirement * 0.9) for seven days at the expense of 0.1 command power per battalion.

Paradrop Order Arrow Tooltip - Hovering over a paradrop arrow will display a tooltip with more detailed order information, as well as alerts if there are insufficient transport wings or the presence of division attrition. The tooltip will not display if hovering over a body of water, only over land.

Once a paradrop executes, the division may suffer losses if its paradrop is disrupted. These losses will be between ⟦0⟧⟦1⟧ to ⟦2⟧⟦3⟧ of the division's strength, including ⟦4⟧⟦5⟧ to ⟦6⟧⟦7⟧ of its ⟦8⟧ and ⟦9⟧⟦10⟧ to ⟦11⟧⟦12⟧ of its equipment, with an additional potential ⟦13⟧ amount of randomness to all factors regardless of the actual amount of disruption. These losses can occur even when the target province is empty, i.e., when it does not have an enemy division in it. Based on repeated tests of the same drop (i.e., the same order form the same save file), such losses do not seem to be dependent on air superiority (i.e., it happens even when at 100% air superiority), but ⟦14⟧ can contribute to how much a division is disrupted.⟦15⟧ Such losses also seem to occur much more frequently when the drop is at higher latitudes (e.g., in Norway or Northern China), or into coastal provinces.

To make paradrops more effective, a player can use the ⟦0⟧ ability with a commander who has the ⟦1⟧ trait. This allows paradropping divisions within the next 7 days to land with a lot more organization (up to ⟦2⟧) and take fewer losses from disruption, though this comes at the cost of Command power.

A Front Line is the starting point of attacks into enemy territory. A player can either assign a whole country's border as a front line by clicking on the border or a player can assign a part of a country's border as a front line by holding the right mouse button and dragging the mouse over the provinces the player wants to belong to the front line deployment area. The AI will then move all the divisions into the position that the commander assigns to that front line. They are assigned either by having them selected when the front line button is clicked or added later by selecting them and Control-Clicking on that line. A player can also create several unconnected front lines and assign divisions between them, which may be particularly useful for a field marshal who may command an unlimited amount of divisions conducting various operations in different locations around the world. Divisions that are stationed at a front line that borders a non-ally will receive a planning bonus for their pre-attack preparation time. Front lines can only be positioned at a border, and the front line of battle between opposing forces counts as a border for this purpose.
For defending an area against partisans, see garrison.

The max planning bonus for each division (⟦0⟧), or the rate of daily planning bonus accumulation, can be increased by certain ⟦1⟧ choices and National Spirits. The base daily gain is ⟦2⟧, so it will take, e.g., 15 days to accumulate to the 30% cap. Using a general will also add both to the max planning bonus and the rate of daily planning bonus accumulation. Each point of a general's planning rating will contribute +2% of max planning bonus, and +5% to the daily planning bonus accumulation. However, the +5% to the daily planning bonus is multiplicative to the 2% daily base rate. So for example, when using a general with a planning rating of 4, they will add +8% to the max planning bonus (so 30% + 8% = 38%, assuming no other bonuses), and the daily planning bonus accumulation will be 2.4% (2% * (1 + (4 * 5% = 20%)) = 2.4%). Continuing the example, it will now take 16 days to complete the full planning bonus (38% / 2.4% = 15.83 days). Commanders, especially field marshals, can also increase the max planning bonus and/or planning speed with certain ⟦3⟧, like ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, and ⟦6⟧. Various ⟦7⟧ can also increase planning speed or max planning bonus, as can officer spirits like ⟦8⟧ and certain political advisors.
To increase the planning bonus in a hurry, the player can use the ⟦0⟧ ability, which can increase the planning speed by ⟦1⟧ for 7 days at the cost of Command power.
